# Configuration

`coop.ini` lives beside the game executable and is parsed by two independent readers that
never talk to each other: the external agent (`src/KotorCoop.Session/CoopConfig.cs`) and the
in-process plugin (`src/KotorCoop.Plugin/PluginConfig.cs` plus direct per-controller reads).
A few keys are read by both sides. The agent's `KotorCoop.Agent` CLI also takes its own
flags, independent of `coop.ini`.

**This page has two tables.** [Player settings](#player-settings) is the entire shipped
`profiles/coop.ini.example` — every key a player would ever want to change, with a plain-
language explanation. [Developer switches](#developer-switches-do-not-change) is everything
else either reader consumes: tuning knobs and bisect levers built for the test rig and for
isolating a specific bug, each one **shipped at its own verified value** and not something a
player needs to touch. Setting one by hand is unsupported — it may reintroduce a bug that was
fixed by flipping it, or regress a measured latency win. Both readers log a line
(`coop.ini: developer switch 'X = value' is set (not a player setting; see docs/CONFIG.md)`)
whenever a coop.ini they load sets one of these, and a similar line for any key neither reader
recognises at all, so a stray or copy-pasted line is never silently in effect with nothing
pointing at it.

**Behaviour-flag negotiation (2026-08-27, extended 2026-09-25).** Twenty-two of the keys below
(and two CLI-only ones, `--no-party-sync` and `--require-identical-save`) are now compared
between the two peers at join time — `coop.ini`/CLI settings used to run purely from local disk
with no way to tell a player their partner had a different value, unlike the game-content
fingerprint further down this doc. A difference is always a **warning** (`W_CFG <key> host=<v>
you=<v>`, once per key, through the same stdout/`~`-console/in-game-overlay path a content
warning uses) — never a refusal, never a dropped channel. For nine keys that gate a channel the
HOST already drives by design, a CLIENT additionally **adopts the host's value at runtime**
rather than keep running its own: `party_sync`, `effect_sync`, `trigger_relay`, `liveness_sync`,
`map_reveal_sync`, `script_item_sync`, `dialogue_item_sync`, `dialogue_recruit_sync`,
`movie_relay`. Four of those nine (`party_sync`, `script_item_sync`, `dialogue_item_sync`,
`movie_relay`) are live-consulted directly by the `KotorCoop.Session` pump that runs the
channel; the other five (`effect_sync`, `trigger_relay`, `liveness_sync`, `map_reveal_sync`,
`dialogue_recruit_sync`) are gated entirely inside the separate PLUGIN process, so adoption for
them crosses that process boundary instead — the agent pushes the adopted bits into the plugin's
shared block every tick they change, and each of the five plugin controllers resolves its
effective value from there instead of its own construction-time `coop.ini` read. All nine are
host-adopted end to end as of 2026-08-27, and all nine are developer switches below, not player
settings. **Two more, `inventory_mode`/`credits_mode` (2026-09-25), follow the identical
host-authoritative-adoption rule** — live-consulted directly by `PartyPoolPumpV2`/`PartyPump`,
same as the four session-side keys above — but unlike the other nine, both are PLAYER settings
(the "Your character" table above), since choosing personal vs. shared inventory is a first-class
gameplay decision, not a tuning knob. See [mod-compatibility.md](research/mod-compatibility.md)'s
"Behaviour-flag negotiation" section for the full design and the exact wire shape, and
[personal-inventory.md](research/personal-inventory.md) for the two newest keys' own design.
Nothing here changes what a key is READ as locally (`CoopConfig`/`AgentSettings` still describe
this install's own coop.ini/CLI exactly as before); adoption lives in a separate, session-scoped
`SessionOverrides` layer.

Every default below is the CODE's own fallback — what applies if the key is absent from
`coop.ini` entirely. **The file that actually ships** (`profiles/coop.ini.example`, staged
verbatim as `coop.ini` by `tools/package.ps1`) sets several keys explicitly, which overrides
the code fallback for anyone using the packaged release. Where the shipped file's value
differs from the code fallback, a footnote says so — that is the value a real install
actually runs with.

**Retired keys.** `combat_state_sync` (a no-op since 2026-08-27 — see
[combat-participation.md](research/combat-participation.md)'s dated section) was removed
entirely from `coop.ini.example`, both readers, and this doc as part of the 2026-09
"player settings vs. developer switches" cleanup; see git history for the old stub
(`CombatStateController.cs`) if you need the archaeology.

fallback (they agree here — `CoopIniExampleDocSyncTests` checks it).

nine host-adopted keys (see "Behaviour-flag negotiation" above), so a HOST who deletes just that
one line advertises OFF in the digest while its own plugin keeps running the channel ON — a real
negotiation mismatch, not just a doc gap.
¹¹ `solo_segment_spectate` is read TWICE off the same key, by two independent readers, the same
split `pazaak_detect`⁹ and `movie_relay`² already use: `CoopConfig.SoloSegmentSpectateEnabled`
(agent side) is what makes `CoopAgent.PumpOnce`'s own peer-visibility filter hide every remote
peer while the local player owns an active segment; `PluginConfig.ReadBool("solo_segment_spectate",
...)` (plugin side, in-process) gates both the owner-side detection that sets the wire flag in
the first place AND the spectator-side reaction (input lock, camera, damage gate) on the OTHER
player's instance. Both default ON as of 2026-08-28 (live-verified via the script-agnostic
`RemovePartyMemberHook` burst trigger — docs/research/star-forge-finale.md §12); setting it to 0
in `coop.ini` turns every half off together. The one remaining unverified half is whether the
input lock stops a real PHYSICAL WASD press — injected keystrokes never reach this game, so only
the levers engaging (the log line, the phantom hide, the parked camera) could be confirmed.
¹² `stun.l.google.com:19302,stun1.l.google.com:19302` — this is `CoopConfig`'s fallback when
the key is entirely absent; a `stun_servers = ` line present but empty is what actually turns
discovery off (see `PublicAddressDiscovery.ParseServers` and `network-topology.md`'s privacy
note — every query is a UDP datagram to a third party).
¹³ Added 2026-08-29 as part of a DLL-level bisect of always-installed plugin pieces
(`docs/research/transition-crashes.md`) — these two, plus the pre-existing
`item_template_spawn_sync`/`status_indicator`/`minigame_wait_notice`/`party_select_host_only`
keys, are every always-on hook/controller/reader added to the plugin since 2026-08-27 that
runs regardless of any other coop.ini feature flag. Diagnostic-only: default ON, meant to stay
ON in a real install, exist purely so a bisection round can isolate one piece at a time.

## CLI flags (`KotorCoop.Agent`, `AgentOptions.cs`)

Commands: `launch`, `load`, `autotrack`, `track`, `run`, `scan`, `info`, `profiles`,
`install-datamods`, `serve-world`, `adopt`, `craft-save`. `run` drives the co-op loop; the
others are setup, discovery or offline utilities. `agent` with no arguments prints help.

| Flag | Default | Meaning | Command(s) |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `--pid <n>` | none | attach by process id | target selection (most commands) |
| `--process <name>` | none | attach by process name, no `.exe` | target selection |
| `--wait` | off | wait for the target process instead of failing immediately | target selection |
| `--profile <name>` | `kotor1` | offset profile to use | `run` |
| `--name <text>` | `player<random>` | player name shown to peers | `run` |
| `--host` | off | host a session | `run` |
| `--join <host[:port]>` | off | join a session | `run` |
| `--port <n>` | `27015`⁶ | listen/target port | `run` |
| `--tick <n>` | `30` | poll and network rate, Hz, clamped 1-60 | `run` |
| `--read-only` | off | attach without write access | `run` |
| `--game-path <path>` | `C:\GOG Games\Star Wars KOTOR (GOG)\swkotor.exe` | game executable (or directory, for `install`/`uninstall`, which auto-detect the GOG install when omitted) | `launch`, `install`, `uninstall` |
| `--windowed` | off | set `FullScreen=0` in `swkotor.ini` first (backed up) | `launch` |
| `--via-steam` | off | launch via `steam://rungameid/32370` instead of the exe | `launch` |
| `--instance <n>` | `1` | co-op instance number, clamped 1-9 (mutex renamed for 2+) | `launch` |
| `--load-save <n>` | `0` (stay at main menu) | load save `n` (1 = top of list) with no input | `launch` |
| `--kotor` | off | use the KOTOR-specific bridge (vtable scan, phantom bodies) | `run` |
| `--no-module-filter` | filter is on | show peers regardless of module | `run` |
| `--no-follow` | follow is on | do not auto-travel to the host's module on join | `run` |
| `--load-via-menu` | off | load saves via menu clicks instead of the in-process replay | `launch`/`load` |
| `--require-identical-save` | off | refuse a peer whose save differs, instead of degrading channels | `run` |
| `--allow-different-save` | n/a | no-op, kept for old scripts (now the default) | `run` |
| `--password <text>` | empty | session password | `run` |
| `--steam-join <s>` | none | join the session named by a Steam rich-presence connect string (`kc1/<host>:<port>[/<token>]`) — what Steam's "Join Game" passes. Decoded into the same host/port/password a typed `--join` would set; a malformed string prints help rather than dialling. Needs no Steam client: it is only a decoder | `run` |
| `--no-party-sync` | sync is on | do not reconcile the party | `run` |
| `--no-progression-sync` | sync is on | do not share gold/XP | `run` |
| `--menu` | off | wait for the in-game Co-op menu button before connecting | `run` |
| `--drop-file <path>` | none | watch a path for a scripted item-drop request | `run` |
| `--log <path>` | none | append a compact status log | `run` |
| `--phantoms <n>` | `4` | idle creatures to claim as remote-player avatars, clamped 0-8 | `run` |
| `--enemy-census-cap <n>` | `0` (built-in 128) | DEBUG: shrink the enemy-census cap, clamped 1-128 | `run` |
| `--source <dir>` | none | save directory to copy from | `craft-save` |
| `--dest <dir>` | none | save directory to create (must not exist) | `craft-save` |
| `--bool <NAME[=0\|1]>` | none, repeatable | force a global boolean; bare `NAME` means `=1` | `craft-save` |
| `--number <NAME=N>` | none, repeatable | force a global number, -128..127 | `craft-save` |

⁶ Applies to a scripted `--host`/`--join` run with no `--port`. An auto-started (`--menu`)
session instead takes its port from `coop.ini`'s own `port` key when `--port` was not passed
(`AgentOptions.PortExplicit` tracks whether the flag was actually given, since `27015` is also
a value someone could type on purpose) — before this was fixed, `--menu` runs silently ignored
`coop.ini`'s `port =` line and always bound `27015`. An explicit `--port` always wins over
`coop.ini`, the same as every other CLI-vs-`coop.ini` precedence in this doc. (The CLI's own
`--tick` help text used to say "(default 20)", stale against the actual
`ProtocolConstants.DefaultTickRate = 30` default; that has since been corrected too.)

## Changes to `swkotor.ini`

Besides `coop.ini`, the plugin sets `[Game Options] EnableCheats=1` in the game's own
`swkotor.ini` so the `~` console works. The first time, it keeps the original file as
`swkotor.ini.kcoop-orig`; `KotorCoop.Agent.exe uninstall` restores the original `EnableCheats`
value from that copy.

Rewritten 2026-08-27 from a six-domain, code-verified audit (combat/companions, shared
world, session/travel/reliability, dialogue/cinematics/minigames, protocol/tests/quality,
player experience) run against the refactored tree. The 2026-08-21 version of this file was
snapshotted before same-day fixes landed and had drifted badly: ten of its rows described
work that was already done. Every row below was checked against the code, not the docs.

Status words: **Verified-live** / **Built (NEEDS-LIVE)** / **Partial** / **Missing** /
**Decision needed**.

Status columns re-synced 2026-09-03 against [status-engineering.md](status-engineering.md), which
is the current source of truth for "does X work" — this file is the history of how each row got
there. When the two disagree, status-engineering.md wins.

time; everything else builds and unit-tests in parallel.

## Tier 1 — what a normal two-player playthrough still hits

| # | Item | Status | Where |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | **Party shared-loot pool (`pt_item_repo`, `CSWPartyTable+0x118`) is two unrelated pools.** Gear stashed "in the party" on one instance never exists on the other. Content-keyed op-log channel built 2026-08-27 (`party_pool_sync`, OFF until live-verified); add/remove both ways, host-relayed, `Set`-based resync on reconnect. Two C#-side echo/timing bugs found and fixed across 2026-08-27/28, but the deeper cause turned out to be native: §16 (2026-08-29) disassembled `CItemRepository::InsertItem` and found an unconditional bail-out on the party pool's own repository flag bit — every deposit through the codebase's own primitive silently no-op'd. Switching to the engine's own `AddItem` (§16's fix) instead **reliably CRASHED the host** (§17, 3/3, `AddItem`'s merge-notify path reaches dead multiplayer network code and dereferences a bad pointer) — worse than the no-op it replaced. §18 fixed it properly: back to `InsertItem`, bracketed by a transient clear of the flag bit for the duration of one call, avoiding both crash triggers by construction. §19 (2026-08-28, rig round) re-ran the crash repro against this fix: **CLOSED, 3/3, plus a warp transition, rapid multi-add both sides, pathological ambient-script stack sizes, and a full blackout/reconnect** — no crash anywhere. Still held OFF: `poolremove` failed to find one ambient-deposited entry (an identity-key mismatch, not a crash) and the rapid-multi-add cross-side aggregate count could not be read cleanly through that round's own ambient module noise. The flip round then re-ran the recipe on the SHIPPED default combination (`dialogue_item_sync`/`script_item_sync` ON, not isolated) and caught one more real cross-channel echo — a party-pool add lands in the PC's own item repository, so `script_item_sync` re-broadcast our own pool applies as fresh script grants and the peer materialised a second copy (closed by `CoopAgent.NoteLocalPartyPoolAdd`). After that: three rapid host deposits mirrored one-for-one, a client deposit and withdrawal each applied exactly once, zero spurious publishes, both instances converging on identical item totals. **`party_pool_sync` now ships ON at mode 2.** | **DONE — ON by default at mode 2 (2026-08-29)** ✅ | `Pumps/PartyPoolPump.cs`/`PartyPoolPumpV2.cs`, `PartyPoolStore.cs`, `Odyssey.PartyPool.cs`, `KotorGameBridge.PartyPool.cs`; docs: [party-pool-sync.md](research/party-pool-sync.md) §16-27, [shared-inventory-v2.md](research/shared-inventory-v2.md) §1-10 |
| 2 | **Items granted by scripts outside dialogue** (OnEnter, OnDeath, cutscene, heartbeat — most quest items) reach only the engine that ran the script. `script_item_sync` pump built 2026-08-27. The container/corpse-loot control DID double-report on its first run — root cause: `PumpContainerLoot` and the script-item sample ran on independently-clocked ~1s timers with no ordering guarantee, so a suppression entry could land after the report it was meant to prevent. Fixed by moving `PumpContainerLoot` onto the fast per-tick path, ordered immediately ahead of the script-item sample (`CoopAgent.PumpOnce`); re-run confirmed clean. Flipped ON by default. | Live-verified ✅ | `Pumps/ScriptItemGrantPump.cs`, `ScriptItemGrantRule`, `Pumps/LootPump.cs`, `CoopAgent.cs` |
| 3 | 🎮 **Progression never live-verified** against a real vendor purchase (gold ledger) or a cross-side kill (XP max-merge). Code is complete. Gold ledger live-verified 2026-08-27 (see `docs/research/progression-sync.md`'s own "Live-verified" section); XP max-merge live-verified 2026-09-02 (a client kill raised the PC's XP 150→300 on both sides, no double-count) — see `docs/research/progression-sync.md`'s "What ships for XP max-merge (2026-09-02)" section for the exact publish/reconcile/rejoin/3-peer rules and citations. A real vendor purchase with a live peer gold contribution mid-browse converged 2026-09-03 after a purse-wrap fix (`GoldReadingRule`, `Odyssey.TryReconcileStoreGoldCache`). | Live-verified ✅ (gold 2026-08-27 + 2026-09-03, XP 2026-09-02) | `Pumps/PartyPump.cs:159-282` |
| 4 | 🎮 **Container-loot race**: two clicks on the same chest within one RTT can both hand out loot before either removal lands (`ContainerUseRule` is eventually consistent). Attempted 2026-08-27: staged both players on a known footlocker position (`end_m01aa`, 10.8/21.87) and fired `useplaceable` on both within ~200ms via `blockpoke.ps1` — refused on both sides, "none close enough / none with inventory", most likely because this container was already emptied by an earlier test round using the same persistent save. Race itself still never exercised. **Fix built 2026-08-27**: host-arbitrated explicit request/response (`LockResponse` packet, `InteractionClaimPacket.RequestSerial`) layered on the same `InteractionLockStore.Claim` decision — `ContainerUseHook` now DEFERS a fresh click (swallows the engine's open, same shape as a peer-held refusal) instead of allowing it outright, asks the host synchronously (in-process for the host's own clicks, one packet round trip for a client), and re-issues the click via `Odyssey.UseObject` within a couple of frames of the grant. Loopback-tested (real host + two real clients, `ContainerLockArbitrationTests.cs`): two simultaneous requests for the same container yield exactly one grant, and the loser can be granted after the winner releases. **Live-verified 2026-08-27/28**: the correct outcome (exactly one winner) confirmed live, then a real fast-path latency bug found (every request timed out at the original 300ms budget, falling back to the pre-fix behaviour) and fixed by raising `ContainerLockArbiter.TimeoutMs` to 1000ms; a same-day re-run confirmed the fast path itself now resolves inside the budget with no fallback on either side. `container_lock_arbitration` stays ON by default — this item is fully closed, correct-outcome AND fast-path-confirmed. | Live-verified ✅ 🎮 | `Pumps/WorldStatePump.cs:24-52`, `ContainerUseRule.cs`, `ContainerUseHook.cs`, `ContainerLockArbiter.cs`, `InteractionLockController.ContainerArbitration.cs`, `CoopHost.InteractionLocks.cs`, `CoopClient.InteractionLocks.cs`; docs: [container-sync.md](research/container-sync.md) §11 |

See `disconnect-reconnect.md` §10 and its follow-up "the fix — PASS" section. | Live-verified: FIXED ✅ 🎮 | `CoopAgent.cs`, `AwayRule`, `KotorGameBridge.Player.cs`, `KotorGameBridge.cs`, `KotorGameBridge.Encounters.cs` |
| 6 | **Protocol-version mismatch used to be silence** (the 15 s "no reply" timeout). Now a typed `E_PROTO` Reject both ways (2026-08-27). | Built | `CoopHost.cs`, `CoopClient.cs`, `PacketCodec.PeekTypeAnyVersion` |
| 7 | **`coop.ini` divergence between peers is unchecked.** ~~Every behaviour flag...~~ Twenty keys (`local_combat`, `party_fast_pump`, the load-rejoin gates, `follow_lead`, `interp_ms` and 16 more) now ride a `BehaviourDigest` in Hello/Welcome (Version 40, 2026-08-27): every difference warns (`W_CFG`) through the same announcer path content warnings use; nine host-authoritative keys (`party_sync`, `effect_sync`, `trigger_relay`, `liveness_sync`, `map_reveal_sync`, `script_item_sync`, `dialogue_item_sync`, `dialogue_recruit_sync`, `movie_relay`) are additionally adopted by the client at runtime via `SessionOverrides` — four of those nine (`party_sync`, `script_item_sync`, `dialogue_item_sync`, `movie_relay`) are live-consulted by their pump; the other five now read through a plugin-side bridge (`EffectiveBehaviourFlag`/`BehaviourOverrideRule`, built the same day in "Closing the plugin-side gap, 2026-08-27") instead of a construction-time bool, but a client's controller actually changing behaviour on adoption has not yet been confirmed on the live rig — see mod-compatibility.md's NEEDS-LIVE item 3. Tick rate's own adoption (2026-08-27, separate mechanism) is unaffected. Live-verified 2026-08-27: a real `party_sync`/`interp_ms` divergence on the rig produced both `W_CFG` lines on both screens, and the client's adopted `party_sync` was confirmed genuinely running (not just logged) via `partystate.ps1`'s `soloMode` read — see mod-compatibility.md's "Live-verified 2026-08-27" section. | Live-verified (core mechanism) 🎮 | `BehaviourDigest.cs`, `BehaviourCompatibility.cs`, `SessionOverrides.cs`, `CoopConfig.cs`, `Packets/SessionPackets.cs`, `BehaviourAnnouncer.cs` |
| 8 | **Fog-of-war reveal** (`map_reveal_sync`) — live-verified 2026-08-27: engine call fires correctly, follows peer movement, survives a module transition with no crash, negligible frame cost. Default ON. Only the on-screen M-key appearance is unconfirmed (screenshot tooling broken). | Verified-live (partial — data path only) | `MapRevealController.cs`, `MapRevealRule.cs` |
| 9 | **Pazaak is invisible to the mod** (GUI panel, not `GetMiniGame`). `pazaak_detect` read built 2026-08-27; negative check live-verified 2026-08-27 (no false positives), positive path (a real hand, via the same-day `pazaak` console verb) run live 2026-08-28: latch, park and the "waiting" toast all PASS. Found and fixed a real bug along the way — the edge detector's range guard silently rejected the literal-`1` flag value a live Pazaak hand actually sets, so detection never fired despite the flag reading correctly through the engine's own `GetPazaakIsRunning`. Ending a hand (the CLEAR direction) remains untested — no console primitive can drive `EndPazaakGame` yet, only a real completed GUI hand reaches it. `pazaak_detect` flipped ON by default. Swoop/turret park-and-hide unchanged; co-visible swoop never observed. | Live-verified ✅ 🎮 | `MinigameController.cs`, `MinigameNoticeRule` |
| 10 | **Companion follow-AI last-waypoint stall — reframed from a bug into a structural fact, then narrowed further.** Two earlier fix candidates (`party_follow_extend_final_node`, `party_follow_advance_destnode_phase6`) stay OFF after a fourth inconclusive live A/B (2026-08-28) — a separate phase=2 idle stall intercepted the companion before either could be judged. Round 98 (static, no rig) named that phase=2 successor phase, phase 7 (`PathWaitDest`, disassembled in full), then proved something bigger by tracing `DriveOne`'s own `ClaimCreature` call through the AI master's outer dispatch gate: **a mirrored companion's follow-AI never runs at all while mirroring holds** — the per-pass reclaim needed so local AI can't contest the driven position also keeps the engine's own follow dispatcher from ever re-entering, so the follow record simply freezes, unread, for the whole mirrored session. This is not a bug to fix; companions on a client are host-driven by design. The frozen record only matters at the boundary where mirroring ENDS — a candidate fix, `party_follow_phase7_release`, resets it to the engine's own watchdog sentinel right there. Round 100 (2026-08-28, rig round) ran the live A/B: control clean as expected, but treatment produced no observable effect either — narrowed to inside `TryReleaseFollowPhaseOnUnmirror` itself (not the config gate, not the tracked-id cache), not root-caused further. Round 101 (static) root-caused it precisely by disassembly: the default-ON, client-only `party_together_fix` clamps the exact field `GetPartyIndexFn`'s search bound reads, hiding the mirrored companion from the lookup deterministically for the whole mirrored session — fixed with a bounded retry against the true, un-clamped count, plus distinct refusal-reason logging on every branch. Round 102 (rig, three reps/leg) confirmed the fix now genuinely EXECUTES (a real `phase7release` log line on all three treatment reps, unlike round 100's silence) but all three landed on "already at the reset sentinel" (-1), never catching a genuinely stuck phase 5/7 — and surfaced a separate, real finding: `reconnect` does not reliably re-mirror a companion the way a fresh `connect` does. Round 103 (static) root-caused THAT reconnect gap to an agent-side `KotorGameBridge` write cache that survives a disconnect (`SessionManager` keeps one bridge alive across every reconnect) and fixed it with an explicit `Reset()` wired into `ClearCoopState()`. Round 104 (rig) confirmed the reconnect fix live: three reconnect reps, all re-mirror within ~2s, no full instance restart needed — that specific gap is closed. `party_follow_phase7_release` itself stays OFF: across every rig rep run against it so far, its corrective branch has never had a genuinely stuck phase to correct. **Round 105 (2026-08-29, rig round) closes it.** Root cause named exactly: `PathWaitDest`'s accept is a STRICT compare, and at the end of a leg the recorded trail node collapses onto `PriorPoint`, so `distSqToPrior` reads a hard 0 and the compare is arithmetically incapable of passing — reproduced 4/4, and shown in its severe form as a leader teleported 16.5 units away that the companion never recovers from.
